selection.rationale: Measured facts. (1) Objective split: ORIGINAL baseline end_to_end_ms 690.12 with ttft_ms 24.05 and decode_ms 666.12 (inputs/project.json), so 96.5% of the objective is the 31 host-bound decode steps at decode-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9 (group 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f, 374.18 ms inclusive diagnostic CUDA over 31 invocations), while the ttft_ms constraint (<=1.05x fresh ORIGINAL TTFT) is decided entirely in the prefill span at prefill-phase call 900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a (group e0861b46dbeeb562f67f, 21.57 ms diagnostic CUDA; adapter _infer inputs/source/opop_adapter.py:32-49). Decode is host-dispatch bound, not kernel bound: execution_timeline (inputs/observations/current/execution_timeline-1221e205.json, revision b61996e1 = current revision) measured a 1441.75 ms profiled window with only 386.81 ms kernel-active union and 1054.37 ms of gaps over 66,441 kernels; python_runtime (python_runtime-aea48e29.json) counted 17,472 _wrapped_call_impl over 32 forwards (~546 Python module dispatches per forward, Qwen3DecoderLayer.forward cumulative 857.97 ms in that perturbed trace). (2) Trial history at exactly this boundary (parent b61996e1): the decode-only CUDA-graph candidate PASSED full quality (max_abs_error 0.0 on 4,861,988 elements across both continuous steps, exact greedy tokens, teacher-forced replay exact) and cut decode_ms 666.12->368.41 and end_to_end_ms 690.12->395.01, but was rejected solely for ttft_ms 26.51/25.92 vs limit 25.2536 (=1.05x24.051052), a systematic +2.0-2.5 ms regression in all 10 samples present in the first repeat: unrepairable from the decode boundary because nothing inside the decode phase lies inside the ttft span, which ends at the first-token torch.cuda.synchronize() before any decode step. (3) The joint trial (trial-a254520daa, inputs/previous-candidate/candidate.py) extended the same verified graph machinery to the prefill span and then failed QUALITY at continuous step 1: AssertionError 'teacher-forced replay token sequence differs from greedy run' (opop_adapter.py:156; evaluator traceback in inputs/previous-feedback.txt parameter_search), with the developer audit showing teacher replay 12/32 tokens differ, first divergence at decode position 1, max_abs 31.125, 459,683 of 4,861,952 logit elements beyond tolerance, while step-0 teacher replay, both greedy runs (bitwise) and step-1 teacher prefill logits were exact. (4) Concrete defect found in the actual implementation, not a generic failure class: candidate.py:561-564 returns the PERSISTENT runner.prefill_mirror view-cache object from the prefill boundary on every invocation, and candidate.py:505-509 trusts object identity ('past is self._mirror') in the decode guard. Route telemetry shows the teacher replay's prefill calls hit the replacement (observe-phase prefill_graph_replay count 2) while its decode calls produced NO replacement routes (run-phase graph_replay count 62 = 2x31 exactly), i.e. the observe-phase decode calls execute the plain parent, which consumes the returned mirror. Verified in the measured worker's transformers 5.16.1 (cache_utils.DynamicLayer.update): 'self.keys = torch.cat([self.keys, key_states], dim=-2)' REBINDS the layer tensors, so the first parent-side use (observe step 0) permanently mutates the persistent mirror away from its master-buffer views; the next teacher replay (observe step 1) receives that same stale object carrying the previous invocation's length-257 K/V and decodes on it - stale exactly from position 256 (= decode position 1), which matches the observed first-divergence position, the large logit error and the exact prefill logits, while greedy runs stay exact because the replacement path reads the masters and checks only identity. (5) Why joint: the repair needs both boundaries as one bundle - the decode boundary carries the quality-proven replay of the 31 host-bound decode steps (96.5% of the objective), the prefill boundary owns the ttft span that rejected the decode-only candidate, and both share one K/V-master state-ownership protocol - so they are mutually dependent edits at the two phase-root module calls. affected_calls is the union of both module subtrees (26,868 calls: prefill root + 3,641 descendants, decode root + 23,225 descendants, disjoint; both group calls included), matching the established convention at this boundary. No multi-process or communication dimension exists (resources.json: single-device task, communication not_applicable).
selection.hypothesis: Repair the single observed failure (teacher-forced replay divergence at continuous step 1) by removing the shared-persistent-cache defect while keeping the previously quality-proven machinery: the 31 per-cache-length decode graphs and the one prefill graph, captured from the parent itself under the capture-blind transformers.masking_utils.is_tracing patch, with static K/V masters and per-build BITWISE verification that permanently falls back to the plain parent on any mismatch. Changes versus trial-a254520daa, all at the same two boundaries: (a) never hand out a persistent cache object - the prefill and decode boundaries return a FRESHLY assembled per-invocation view-cache of the masters (pure Python views, correct get_seq_length), so any caller-side DynamicLayer.update rebinding dirties only that invocation's object and nothing is reused across invocations; (b) never trust persistent identity - the decode guard resolves the step from the caller's past_key_values BY VALUE (layer count, per-layer shape/dtype/device, advertised length consistent with the expected step), refreshing the master prefix from the caller's own tensors when the cache was parent-produced, with identity allowed only as a shortcut for this invocation's own fresh mirror; any mismatch replays nothing and routes the remainder of that invocation to the plain parent (eager, correct); (c) keep mixed routing correct: the audit's route differential (observe-phase prefill replaced, observe-phase decode absent) says caller decode calls may execute the plain parent on the cache we return - on a fresh mirror that is exactly the eager parent on this invocation's just-replayed masters, reproducing the bitwise-exact behavior already observed at step 0; if such a parent-produced cache is later threaded back into the replacement, the value-based guard refreshes the masters from it (or falls back) so no path reads stale K/V. The ttft repair is unchanged in design: replaying the prefill span removes its ~2.4 ms host overhead over 21.57 ms of prefill CUDA busy time and both candidate mechanisms of the prior +2.0-2.5 ms regression (allocator interaction, post-replay clock state) are addressed by owning the span; the constraint baseline is the evaluator's fresh ORIGINAL measurement, so margin, not equality, is the target. Expected effect, to be tested by the framework's fresh measurement: end_to_end_ms ~391-395 ms (vs 690.12 ORIGINAL, ~43% lower) with decode_ms ~368 ms and ttft_ms at or below a ~24.05 fresh original against the ~25.25 limit. Falsifiable predictions: (i) continuous step-1 teacher-forced replay returns exact tokens and logits within 0.02/0.02 - the previous failure no longer reproduces; (ii) both continuous steps' greedy runs stay bitwise exact (32 tokens, full last-position logits); (iii) fresh evaluator ttft median <= 1.05x fresh original ttft; (iv) any verification or guard failure degrades to plain-parent execution and still passes quality (slower, never silently wrong numerics). Explicit unknowns retained: which mechanism dominated the prior ttft regression is not resolved by evidence; whether the framework routes observe-phase decode calls through the replacement is evidenced only by the route-telemetry differential, so the repair makes both routings correct rather than depending on either; the 374.18 ms decode CUDA time is nested/inclusive diagnostic time, not additive with prefill or wall time.

review.delivery: Exact selector snapshot changes only routed supplemental_evidence. Both selector and candidate read facts; downstream selection differs, so candidate is not a same-snapshot one-variable A/B. One success is not stable causal superiority. External filesystem is accessible.
review.code: Fresh cache/layer objects per return, request reset, value/length-aware prefix refresh, separate prefill pool and direct replacement greedy/teacher self-checks. These jointly differ from a866; no unique cause isolated. Direct self-checks bypass framework signature dispatch; actual external evaluator passes, not self-check assertions, establish tested quality.
review.scope: One joint bundle covers prefill and decode, not multiple-bundle coexistence. One round means no post-accept rediscovery. Corrected-interface developer-factual continuation with prior manual external source mapping, not unaided original-entry success.
review.probes: Two CPU fixture errors (cache length then assertion shape) retained, final fake-cache/value/reset guards passed. No full CUDA quality from CPU probes. Selector timeline inspection had a type error. All roles zero schema repairs.
review.collectors: Native SQLite independently recomputed for current code. Separate profile, never acceptance timing. Timeline unions/gaps cannot be subtracted from clean scores as isolated host cost. Binding ablation compares whole parent/passthrough workers without candidate build/computation, and yielded negative deltas: not negative physical binding cost or group-specific attribution. Run-only diagnostics do not certify quality.
review.limits: Temporary global capture patch/concurrent composition and arbitrary ownership are not generically certified. Source numeric mapping only covers full tokens/logits. Lifetime memory increased; not a memory gain. Original TTFT anchor is25.2536046. Preserve old failures.
review.next: Independent full-version AB/BA against original controls/baseline, publish=False, reviewed source identity check, and a separate baseline native profile. Reuse already collected current-candidate native evidence; no new search or repeated acceptance.
